commits.message:
Address Qodo round 2: avoid the status-prefix trim trap, retry comment/relabel

Reads the private worktree's changed paths from three plain path
lists (two diffs, one ls-files) instead of git status --porcelain,
so the shared git helper's whole-output trim can no longer eat a
leading status character and shift a path's prefix. The blocked-run
comment and its corrective relabel each get one retry on their own,
so a transient failure in either no longer silently leaves a blocked
run looking agent-done with nothing said about it.

Address Qodo round 1: check before committing, no-renames, redaction

Lists changed paths from the untracked/committed working tree before
any add/commit, so the check runs ahead of the commit it gates.
Disables rename detection so a protected file moved under the evidence
root still shows its old path as changed. Drops the path trim that let
a leading space slip a root-level path past the prefix check. Retries
the quarantine push. Keeps the recovery branch or folder name in the
ticket comment even when the blocked paths themselves must be
redacted, posts it before the corrective relabel, and only keeps a
blocked run's worktrees when even that branch push failed.

Refuse to publish private evidence outside its allowed paths

The runner pushed whatever the agent left in the private worktree
straight to main. Now it diffs the private branch against origin/main
first: a run that changed anything outside raw-artifacts/ or
factory-log/ is kept on its own branch instead, main never moves, and
the ticket is marked agent-needs-help with the paths named.

Fix four review findings: unfinished public tests, silent kills, and the audit's pull-request scan

- inject: a bug case with no evidence on its public tests (not_run) is
  now unvalidated too, not just a control; previously only a control
  checked that outcome.
- inject: a run's step log always names its outcome, including the
  signal that killed it when there's no spawn error, instead of only
  printing a detail when `result.error` happened to be set.
- factory audit: replace the paginated-then-filtered PR list with
  pullsSince(), which pages by hand, newest first, and stops as soon
  as a page is older than the run window. Reads every pull in the
  window without downloading a repo's whole PR history.
- The source-text regression test for the old approach is replaced
  with direct tests of pullsSince's stopping behaviour.

Give each tooling exit code and recorded result one meaning

ticket:ready now exits 2 when gh fails to read the ticket, distinct from
exiting 1 when the ticket itself is not ready, and its gh call carries a
time limit. inject records a proof or public-test run that hit its time
limit or couldn't be spawned as not_run, never fail, and refuses to
validate on it. rules-evidence skips a stray file that matches the
review-folder pattern instead of crashing. rules-propose drops its
unused mode parameter. The factory audit's PR-reviews read now reads
every page instead of stopping at the first 50.

Closes #114

Factory run: wait for Qodo in the foreground, and no wakeup tool

Run 20261110-150249 for ticket 18 built its change and opened the PR, then
started review:wait as a background task, scheduled a wakeup and ended its
turn. In a headless run that ends the run: the runner read no result and
the task was killed before it saved the review.

The runner's instructions now say to run review:wait in the foreground with
the Bash tool's longest timeout and --timeout 9, to run it again while it
exits 1, and never to start it in the background or schedule a wakeup,
because ending the turn ends the run. agentArgs passes --disallowedTools
ScheduleWakeup, and the factory skill's wait step says the same.
Factory run instructions: give the ticket file's path and rule out listing the environment

Factory tick: verify a stale lock's content before acting on it

Reading a stale lock's pid and then acting on that read are two
separate steps, so another tick could have already moved the same
stale lock away and taken a fresh one of its own in between. Without
a check, this tick's own rename would isolate that fresh lock by
mistake instead of the stale one it actually read, and both ticks
would end up believing they hold it.

The rename's result is now checked against exactly the bytes read
before deciding the lock was stale, and restored if they no longer
match, rather than ever proceeding on a lock that turned out to
belong to someone else.

Factory tick: fix Qodo's round-2 findings on the lock and label changes

- acquireLock no longer uses a second mutex directory to gate stale-lock
  recovery (that directory could itself be reclaimed unsafely by two
  ticks at once). Taking over a stale lock now moves the old file out
  of the way with renameSync instead: renaming is exclusive on its own
  source path, so only one tick's rename of the same stale file can
  ever succeed, and the loser reports busy, not a double claim.
- relabel no longer conflates a failed removal (cosmetic, an old label
  left lingering) with a failed add (the ticket's new state was never
  recorded at all): it now reports each separately. The tick only logs
  and continues past a failed removal; a failed add still stops the
  run, so a claim that didn't really land can't let the agent start,
  and a finish that didn't really land can't be reported as finished.
- The finish step and the fallback both now also strip ready-for-agent,
  not just agent-working, so a ticket whose claim removal failed can't
  end up looking pickable again once the run is actually done.
- Moved the one test that spans a real process into the integration
  suite, where process-spawning tests belong.

Factory tick: fix Qodo's round-1 findings on the label and lock changes

- relabel no longer aborts the whole label update when removing the old
  label fails for a real reason: it still adds the new one, and only
  then reports the removal problem, extracted into a pure relabelWith
  so the retry-after-add behaviour is covered directly. The tick itself
  never lets that problem stop a ticket from getting its final label or
  its comment: the claim, the finish, and the fallback all treat a
  failed relabel as something to log, not something that aborts.
- acquireLock no longer crashes when a fresh tick's own plain lock write
  lands in the narrow gap a stale takeover needs between clearing the
  old lock and writing its own: that now reports busy too.
- The recovery mutex that gates a stale takeover is itself reclaimable
  once clearly too old for its own section to still be running, so a
  crash in that narrow window can no longer block every later tick.
- The PR a timed-out run reports on the ticket is now checked against
  the ticket's own repo, the same way a normal result already is.

Factory tick: time limits on every gh and git call

Every gh and git call in the tick ran with no time limit, so a single
hung call could hold the lock until the job was killed, leaving a
ticket stuck as agent-working with nothing to pick it up again.

- gh and git calls now carry a time limit (60s default, 10 minutes for
  a push or a fetch/clone), and a failed call is reported by name.
- A timed-out call during the audit or the verify step already ends
  the run as agent-needs-help through the existing error handling;
  added tests pin that down now that these calls can actually fail.
- relabel no longer swallows every failed label removal as "already
  gone": only gh's own 404 for a missing label is, everything else
  (403, a different 404, a timeout) is reported.
- Two ticks that both find the same stale lock can no longer both take
  it over: a second, atomic mutex gates the stale-lock recovery path,
  so the loser reports busy.
- A run that hits the time limit after the agent opened a pull request
  now reports that PR in the ticket comment, read from the agent's own
  `gh pr create` step instead of its (missing) final result line.
